hook.text: Plastic from corn — polylactic acid is a biodegradable polymer made entirely from fermented plant sugars.

buildup.text: Bacteria ferment glucose into lactic acid — which is then polymerized into PLA, a transparent, compostable plastic.

discovery.text: NatureWorks produces 150,000 tons of PLA per year — used in cups, packaging, and 3D printing filaments.

twist.text: PLA only biodegrades in industrial composters at 58°C — it persists in landfills and oceans just like regular plastic.

climax.text: Blending PLA with other biopolymers improves heat resistance and flexibility — engineering better bioplastics for real-world use.

punchline.text: Grown, fermented, molded — PLA proves plastics can come from plants, not petroleum.

quiz.question: Why doesn't PLA solve ocean plastic pollution?
options: PLA is toxic to marine organisms
PLA only biodegrades at high temperatures in industrial composters, not in oceans or landfills
PLA dissolves too quickly, making it useless for packaging

details.summary: Polylactic acid is a biodegradable bioplastic made from fermented plant starch, typically corn. It is the most commercially successful bioplastic, used in packaging, disposable cups, 3D printing filament, and medical implants like dissolvable sutures and drug delivery devices.
details.whyItMatters: PLA demonstrates that bio-based plastics can achieve commercial scale. As the highest-volume bioplastic produced globally, it provides a renewable alternative to petroleum plastics for many single-use and medical applications.
takeaways: PLA is made from corn starch fermented into lactic acid then polymerized
It is the most commercially produced bioplastic worldwide
PLA biodegrades in industrial composting but not in home compost or oceans

faq.question: Does PLA biodegrade in home compost or the ocean?
faq.answer: No. PLA requires industrial composting with sustained temperatures above 58 degrees Celsius to break down efficiently. It persists in home compost, landfills, and marine environments for years, similar to conventional plastics in those conditions.

faq.question: How is polylactic acid manufactured from corn?
faq.answer: Corn starch is hydrolyzed to glucose, which bacteria ferment into lactic acid. The lactic acid is purified and polymerized into long PLA chains through either direct condensation or ring-opening polymerization of lactide. The entire process uses renewable feedstock.
